calls.price_at_call: $524 (stated current); DCF fair value $447 (stated) — slightly overvalued on his DCF
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 5 Oct, after downgrading from an excellent-buying-opportunity ranking earlier this year; no flip) — he owns Microsoft (added around $400 in February, after a low near $350), is not interested in selling, and is also not interested in buying before the 28 Oct earnings release because at $524 the risk/reward does not compensate for print risk.
calls.base_case: Most recent reported quarter (29 Jul): revenue $90bn, up 18% year over year (the operating-income increase figure drops out of the captions); forward P/E 22.1, below the stock's own average on that metric; Microsoft's AI segment is growing over 40%.
calls.bull_case: He thinks analyst earnings growth forecasts (the figure drops out of the captions, around 15%) underestimate — he expects closer to 20% EPS growth; backlog approaching $500bn (unit drops out of the captions) and Microsoft may be the only hyperscaler free-cash-flow positive through fiscal 2027.
calls.bear_case: Backlog concentration in OpenAI is a key risk, its own-chip programme trails Alphabet and Amazon, AI investment has flattened operating leverage, and peers may fund the race with dilutive equity (he reads Meta's new share class that way).

calls.thesis: Downgraded from high-conviction BUY (entered <$400, reiterated at $350) after the run to ~$525; DCF fair value ~$406 vs price ~$525 — valuation stretched; not adding above $500 until fundamentals step up, not selling, will hold long-term.
